```{r} #| label: setup #| message: false #| warning: false #| include: false library(tidyverse) library(scales) library(knitr) library(kableExtra) # fonts ---- library(extrafont) library(sysfonts) source("_common.R") # use font showtext::showtext_auto() # set theme ggplot2::theme_set(fmggp2::theme_jurassic( base_size = 15)) ``` ```{r} #| label: status #| results: "asis" #| echo: false # status ---- # polishing, restructuring, drafting, complete status("complete") ``` :::: {.callout-note collapse="false" icon=false} ::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #02577A;"} **Requirements:** ::: ::: {style="font-size: 1.05em; color: #282b2d;"} **✅ a categorical variable** ::: ::: {style="font-size: 1.05em; color: #282b2d;"} **✅ a numeric (continuous) variable** :::
```{r} #| label: full_code_display #| eval: true #| echo: false #| warning: false #| message: false #| out-height: '60%' #| out-width: '60%' #| fig-align: right library(ggplot2) library(dplyr) set.seed(1993) jp_dinos <- tibble( species = c("Brachiosaurus", "Triceratops", "Tyrannosaurus", "Gallimimus", "Velociraptor"), n = c(3, 5, 2, 20, 8), mean_tons = c(40, 9, 8, 0.45, 0.15), sd_tons = c(5, 1.2, 1, 0.08, 0.03)) |> tidyr::uncount(n) |> mutate(weight_tons = round(rnorm(n(), mean = mean_tons, sd = sd_tons), 2)) |> select(species, weight_tons) jp_paddocks <- jp_dinos |> group_by(species) |> summarise(total_tons = sum(weight_tons)) |> ungroup() labs_grp_col <- labs( title = "Jurassic Park", caption = "Simulated data", subtitle = "Total weight of the dinosaurs in each paddock", x = "Paddock", y = "Total weight (tons)") ggp2_grp_col <- ggplot(data = jp_paddocks, aes(x = species, y = total_tons)) + geom_col(aes(fill = species), show.legend = FALSE) + scale_x_discrete(guide = guide_axis(n.dodge = 2)) ggp2_grp_col + labs_grp_col ``` :::: ## Description Grouped bar graphs compare multiple values across categories. Each category has a cluster of bars. X-axis labels show categories and y-axis values. Colors or patterns differentiate subsets, and a legend is shown on the side or top of the graph. `geom_col()` allows us to display 'grouped' numerical values across levels (or groups) of a categorical variable. ## Set up ::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"} **PACKAGES:** ::: Install packages. ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ```{r} #| label: pkg_code_grp_col #| code-fold: show #| eval: false #| echo: true #| warning: false #| message: false #| results: hide library(ggplot2) library(dplyr) # for tibble() and data manipulation library(tidyr) # for uncount() ``` ::: ::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"} **DATA:** ::: In *Jurassic Park* (1993), every species lives in its own paddock. We'll simulate the weight of every dinosaur in the park: each species gets a head count (`n`) and its own normal distribution of weights (`mean_tons` and `sd_tons`). `tidyr::uncount()` repeats each row `n` times (one row per dinosaur), and `rnorm()` draws each dinosaur's weight. Then we add up the weights in each paddock (`total_tons`). Setting the seed with `set.seed()` means you'll get the same dinosaurs every time you run the code below. ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ```{r} #| label: data_code_grp_col #| code-fold: show #| eval: true #| echo: true set.seed(1993) jp_dinos <- tibble( species = c("Brachiosaurus", "Triceratops", "Tyrannosaurus", "Gallimimus", "Velociraptor"), n = c(3, 5, 2, 20, 8), mean_tons = c(40, 9, 8, 0.45, 0.15), sd_tons = c(5, 1.2, 1, 0.08, 0.03)) |> tidyr::uncount(n) |> mutate(weight_tons = round(rnorm(n(), mean = mean_tons, sd = sd_tons), 2)) |> select(species, weight_tons) jp_paddocks <- jp_dinos |> group_by(species) |> summarise(total_tons = sum(weight_tons)) |> ungroup() glimpse(jp_paddocks) ``` ::: ## Distribution A grouped bar graph shows one number per group, and here that number is a total. Totals depend on two things: how many dinosaurs live in a paddock and how much each one weighs. Twenty Gallimimus still weigh less than two Tyrannosaurs. Below we'll move from the dinosaurs, to a picture, to the formula. ::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"} **COUNT IT:** ::: Start with the first six dinosaurs. ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ```{r} #| label: count_values_grp_col #| code-fold: show #| eval: true #| echo: true head(jp_dinos, 6) ``` ::: Each Brachiosaurus weighs close to 40 tons, and each Triceratops weighs close to 9. For every paddock, the total is the number of dinosaurs times their average weight. ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ```{r} #| label: count_summary_grp_col #| code-fold: show #| eval: true #| echo: true jp_dinos |> group_by(species) |> summarise( dinosaurs = n(), mean_tons = mean(weight_tons), total_tons = sum(weight_tons)) ``` ::: ::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"} **DRAW IT:** ::: Each bar in a grouped bar graph is a bar model: a total made of parts. Below we draw every dinosaur as its own segment and stack the segments in each paddock. The height of each stack is the paddock's total, and the number of segments is its head count. The Gallimimus bar has 20 thin segments, and the Brachiosaurus bar has three thick ones. ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ```{r} #| label: draw_grp_col #| code-fold: show #| eval: true #| echo: true ggplot(data = jp_dinos, aes(x = species, y = weight_tons, fill = species)) + geom_col(color = "#111111", linewidth = 0.3, show.legend = FALSE) + scale_x_discrete(guide = guide_axis(n.dodge = 2)) + labs(x = "Paddock", y = "Total weight (tons)") ``` ::: ::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"} **NAME IT:** ::: Each dinosaur's weight comes from a [normal distribution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Normal_distribution) for its species, $X_i \sim \text{Normal}(\mu, \sigma)$. A paddock's total adds up $n$ of these weights: $$ T = X_1 + X_2 + \dots + X_n \sim \text{Normal}(n\mu, \; \sqrt{n}\,\sigma) $$ The expected total is $n\mu$: $3 \times 40 = 120$ tons for the Brachiosaurus paddock and $20 \times 0.45 = 9$ tons for Gallimimus. The spread grows with $\sqrt{n}$, not $n$, because heavy and light dinosaurs partly cancel each other out. Our Brachiosaurus paddock weighs `r round(sum(jp_dinos$weight_tons[jp_dinos$species == "Brachiosaurus"]), 1)` tons, within one standard deviation ($\sqrt{3} \times 5 \approx 8.7$ tons) of its expected 120. Try changing the head counts in `n`. Doubling the Velociraptors doubles their bar, but the bar would still be the shortest in the park. ## Grammar ::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"} **CODE:** ::: Grouped bar graphs assume the statistical measure (i.e., the value that the length of the bars will be derived from) is contained in a variable and mapped to the `x` or `y` aesthetic. - Create labels with `labs()` - Initialize the graph with `ggplot()` and provide `data` - Map `species` to the `x` and `total_tons` to the `y` - Map `species` to `fill` *inside* the `aes()` of `geom_col()` - Stagger the long paddock names over two lines with `scale_x_discrete(guide = guide_axis(n.dodge = 2))` ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ```{r} #| label: code_graph_grp_col #| code-fold: show #| eval: false #| echo: true #| warning: false #| message: false #| out-height: '100%' #| out-width: '100%' labs_grp_col <- labs( title = "Jurassic Park", caption = "Simulated data", subtitle = "Total weight of the dinosaurs in each paddock", x = "Paddock", y = "Total weight (tons)") ggp2_grp_col <- ggplot(data = jp_paddocks, aes(x = species, y = total_tons)) + geom_col(aes(fill = species), show.legend = FALSE) + scale_x_discrete(guide = guide_axis(n.dodge = 2)) ggp2_grp_col + labs_grp_col ``` ::: ::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"} **GRAPH:** ::: ```{r} #| label: create_graph_grp_col #| eval: true #| echo: false #| warning: false #| message: false #| out-height: '100%' #| out-width: '100%' #| layout-nrow: 1 labs_grp_col <- labs( title = "Jurassic Park", caption = "Simulated data", subtitle = "Total weight of the dinosaurs in each paddock", x = "Paddock", y = "Total weight (tons)") ggp2_grp_col <- ggplot(data = jp_paddocks, aes(x = species, y = total_tons)) + geom_col(aes(fill = species), show.legend = FALSE) + scale_x_discrete(guide = guide_axis(n.dodge = 2)) ggp2_grp_col + labs_grp_col ``` ## More info We didn't have to calculate `total_tons` (displayed on the `y` axis) by `species` because `ggplot2` does this for us! If we pass a categorical variable to the `x` (like `species`) and a continuous variable to `y` (like `weight_tons`), `geom_col()` stacks the rows in each group, which adds up `y` for each level of `x`: ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ```{r} #| label: create_summary_sum_col_graph #| eval: true #| echo: true #| warning: false #| message: false jp_dinos |> ggplot(aes(x = species, y = weight_tons)) + geom_col(aes(fill = species), show.legend = FALSE) + scale_x_discrete(guide = guide_axis(n.dodge = 2)) + labs_grp_col ``` ::: We can see the underlying totals using `dplyr`'s `group_by()` and `summarise()` functions. ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ```{r} #| label: create_summary_sum_col #| eval: false #| echo: true #| warning: false #| message: false jp_dinos |> dplyr::group_by(species) |> dplyr::summarise( `Total weight (tons)` = sum(weight_tons) ) |> dplyr::ungroup() |> dplyr::select(`Paddock` = species, `Total weight (tons)`) ``` ::: ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ```{r} #| label: show_summary_sum_col #| eval: true #| echo: false #| warning: false #| message: false #| layout-nrow: 1 jp_dinos |> dplyr::group_by(species) |> dplyr::summarise( `Total weight (tons)` = sum(weight_tons) ) |> dplyr::ungroup() |> dplyr::select(`Paddock` = species, `Total weight (tons)`) |> knitr::kable() |> kableExtra::kable_minimal() ``` :::
